title: Throttle handoff ripple to stop deep queue lockups
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (Hosted + Dedicated + Private) reported P95/P99 token latency regressions and prolonged recovery windows during mixed-length traffic surges. Root cause analysis found a handoff ripple in the admission->dispatcher->worker lease exchange that allowed bursty handoffs to drive deep-queue lockups: a short cascade where many long-context requests simultaneously returned 'lease-granted' and were accepted by the dispatcher, then caused eviction/kv-churn and admission starvation for short requests for several seconds. This manifested as sustained tail latency for latency-sensitive flows and triggered customer escalations (see Acme Health ticket and Escalation #1831).

Impact: High. Affected hosted API tenants in us-west-2 intermittently and several Dedicated customers under mixed workload patterns. Symptoms: sudden spike in P99 generation latency (+200-800ms), queue depth growth to 10-20x normal for 5-30s, customer-visible errors when internal soft-queue capacity was exhausted. Incident windows correlated with deployment waves and private upgrade windows.

Root cause: A race between the admission controller's burst accounting and the worker handoff lease semantics. When a long-context wave was admitted, the handoff protocol would grant leases in tight succession without sufficient smoothing. The dispatcher did not apply backpressure quickly enough and its inflight-window accounting erroneously double-counted partially-handled handoffs under certain ack reorderings. The combination produced a feedback loop: more leases => deeper queue => KV eviction pressure => prefetch/quarantine thrash => admission backoff => starvation of short requests.

Immediate mitigation (hotfix): Implement a conservative per-worker handoff-rate cap and a short randomized jitter on lease grants to break synchronous bursts. Added an emergency admission expiry of 1500ms to ensure stale handoff intents are reclaimed. These were shipped as a hotfix branch to runtime with a staged rollout to Dedicated pools and then Hosted. Hotfix PR: runtime PR#1892 (links below).

Planned fix (post-incident): 1) Replace naive lease grant bursts with a token-bucket backed pacing algorithm that enforces steady handoff throughput under mixed-length loads. 2) Make inflight-window accounting idempotent on duplicate/late acks to avoid double-counting. 3) Introduce a short-term admission hysteresis that prefers short requests when simultaneous admission pressure is detected. 4) Add per-tenant HandoffRate telemetry and a new alarm for HandoffBurstRatio>0.2.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for lease reordering, integration tests added in the local fuzzer suite to simulate mixed-length ingress waves. Added a new canary harness that replays customer traffic profiles (Acme Health and BetaBank profiles). Load tests show median latency neutral, P99 down by ~40% on synthetic mixed waves vs. pre-patch.

Rollout plan: 1) Hotfix rollout (completed to 15% Dedicated pools) -> monitor for 30m -> widen to 50% if stable. 2) Apply to Hosted region us-west-2 at low-traffic window. 3) Coordinate with Private upgrade windows: provide patch and a backout script to customers. 4) After 72h of stable telemetry, merge full pacing algorithm and enable via feature-flag for gradual ramp.

Monitoring and metrics: Added HandoffGrantRate, HandoffBurstRatio, DispatcherInflightWindow, InflightDoubleCountRate, KV-eviction-rate-per-host, ShortRequestDropRate. Dashboards and alerts created. Post-deploy we expect HandoffBurstRatio to drop below 0.05 under normal bursty traffic.

Follow-ups: a) Design a long-term admission policy that factors tokenized cost and SLA class. b) Evaluate making the dispatcher preemptible for short requests. c) Customer outreach and runbook updates.
